newsitem.title: USA: Massachusetts kicks off drive to improve seaports.
newsitem.headline: Massachusetts kicks off drive to improve seaports.

text.p: Massachusetts on Friday said that it was starting its drive to improve its seaports with a $110,000 grant for the port of Salem as part of a program that eventually includes selling around $300 million of bonds.

In addition to the engineering study for Salem, the list of near-term projects includes more than $500,000 for Gloucester, Salem, Fall River and New Bedford, said Richard Armstrong, the executive director of the Seaport Council. The council is an advisory group.
The start of the program was announced on Friday by Lieutenant Governor Paul Cellucci, who held a news conference in Salem.

The state hopes to start an electronic fish auction three or four months from now, which it expects will help raise prices by making it easier for potential purchasers around the world to bid for the catch.

The Seaport Bond Bill, which was approved this summer, includes $100 million for coastal facilities, like docks and warehouses, approximately $100 million for dredging, and another $100 million to improve rail links.
At present, Massachusetts cannot handle double-stacked containers, a limitation it plans to correct.

However, the program will be funded on a pay-as-you-go basis, Armstrong said. "You basically put off selling the bonds until you really need the cash in the harbor," he explained, adding that the first sorts of projects being undertaken, like feasibility studies, are much less costly than some of the ones that will begin later on, like dredging harbors.
